newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM unions say one-off bonus not enough.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM unions say one-off bonus not enough.

text.p: Trade unions in Poland's KGHM copper concern, in a wage rise dispute with the board, accepted on Monday the board's offer of a one-off bonus, but said they would not drop demands of an increase in monthly wages.

KGHM's two major trade unions, Solidarity and the Union of Copper Industry Workers (ZZPPM), demand an increase of monthly wages by up to 150 zlotys for 27,000 workers employed directly in production. The average monthly wage at the compamy is about 2,000 zlotys and the average wage in Poland was 958 zlotys a month in September.
"We have agreed to accept the board's offer of a 250 zloty one-off bonus, but this does not settle our wage dispute," Ryszard Zbrzyzny, head of the ZZPPM told Reuters.

Zbrzyzny said the bonus would take average wage growth in the company to 21.83 percent this year, in line with the agreement reached by the three-sided committee of government, employers and unions for 1996.

But he said unions in KGHM had reached a separate, better deal with the board, linking wages in the firm to the growth of wages in the enterprise sector, where salaries grew more than six percent since July when the dispute started.
KGHM, one of the world's major copper and silver producers, is slated for privatisation in the second quarter of 1997.
The value of the concern, employing a total of 42,500, is estimated at $2-3 billion. Its shares are to be floated both on the international and domestic markets.
